records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — Limiting the top-level domain to five letters rejects valid hosts such as example.technology and prevents configuring their embedding relationships.
records.rationale: The diff shows in app/models/embeddable_host.rb line 2 a regex validation: `validates_format_of :host, :with => /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`. The `[a-z]{2,5}` part limits TLDs to 2-5 characters. Valid TLDs like .museum (6 chars) or .technology (10 chars) would be rejected by this regex. records.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6 lines 42-48, the delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => {...})` without a `.catch()` handler. Looking at the diff, the save action on line 36-38 properly handles errors with `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, but the delete action on lines 42-47 only has a `.then()` callback with no error handling. If the DELETE request fails, the promise rejection would be unhandled and the user would not see any error message, leaving the UI in an inconsistent state.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Unescaped legacy host values are interpolated into SQL, so a URL path containing an apostrophe breaks the upgrade and crafted stored values can alter the statement.
records.rationale: The migration at line 25 uses string interpolation to insert host values directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. The variable `h` comes from splitting the legacy `embeddable_hosts` site setting value by newlines. If any host value contains a single quote (apostrophe), it would break the SQL syntax. More critically, if malicious data was stored in the site setting, it could lead to SQL injection. This is a real security/correctness bug in the migration code.
